role: MEASUREMENT ONLY. This file records a sweep. It repairs nothing, seals nothing, advances no status and accepts no product. It is not an input to any checker and pins no artifact.
scope: Every artifacts/check-*.py in docs/coop as of this sweep (92 files).

method.question: For every checker: does every JSON parse it performs pass an object_pairs_hook (or otherwise reject duplicate object keys); is it exploitable in practice; and which of its inputs are exposed.
method.whyItMatters: json.loads without object_pairs_hook keeps the LAST of duplicate keys. A document can therefore carry a key twice so that a human reader (and any first-wins reader) sees one value while every instrument sees another, with the parsed object byte-identical to the honest one.
method.isolation: docs/coop was copied to a scratchpad and six independent worker trees were made from the copy. Every mutation and every checker execution happened in those copies. No file under the real docs/coop was modified. The only write under docs/coop is this file.

instruments.name: static AST sweep
instruments.what: ast.parse of each checker; locates json.loads/json.load, from-json import aliases, json.JSONDecoder(...) construction, .decode/.raw_decode on a decoder bound to a variable or called inline, and getattr(json,'loads')(...). Records whether object_pairs_hook was supplied. object_pairs_hook=None is counted as UNHOOKED, not hooked.

instruments.name: dynamic decode probe
instruments.what: Each checker was re-executed under runpy with json.loads, json.load, JSONDecoder.decode and JSONDecoder.raw_decode wrapped. Every decode actually executed was recorded with its caller file:line, whether a non-None object_pairs_hook was in effect, and a sha256 of the text decoded so the decode could be attributed back to a file on disk. An audit hook recorded every file opened for reading. This is what makes transitive exposure visible: a checker that closed the class in its own source still executes its predecessors' unhooked parses when it imports them.

instruments.name: live exploit
instruments.what: A duplicate member was inserted into a real input artifact in a worker tree and the checker re-run. Artifact-only, one file, one insert, no checker edit.

attackShapes.A-front-insert: Insert "<key>": <planted>, immediately after the top-level '{'. Last-wins parse is identical to the honest document; key ORDER changes.
attackShapes.C-order-preserving: Insert "<key>": <planted>, immediately before the real member at the same nesting level. Last-wins parse is identical AND dict key insertion order is identical, so an ordered-key comparison against the honest document cannot see it either. This is the stronger shape and is the one the verdicts use.
attackShapes.nested: Same as C but at an arbitrary dotted path, used to confirm the class is not confined to top-level keys.

classification.ADMITTED: exit 0, or (for a checker already red at baseline) output byte-identical to baseline, meaning the instrument never observed the edit at all.
classification.REJECTED-BY-DUPLICATE-KEY-GUARD: non-zero AND a NEW finding line reports a duplicate/DUPKEY/'published more than once' condition. Sub-split by whether that line NAMES the duplicated key.
classification.REJECTED-COLLATERAL: non-zero for any other reason. Sub-split into DIGEST-PIN (a sha/pin/drift comparison), KEY-ORDER (an ordered-key comparison) and OTHER.

method.whyExitCodeAloneWasNotUsed: Every mutant run was diffed against the checker's own baseline run and classified on the NEW finding text. Two positions (check-d9-v1.7.py over d9-exit-contract.v1.7.json and over d9-exit-contract.v1.6.json) return non-zero under attack shape A and would read as 'defended' on the exit code alone. The finding is D18 'successor differs outside the closed v1.7 delta; first difference: $: ordered keys [...]' — a key-ORDER comparison, not a duplicate-key guard. Under the order-preserving shape C both positions are ADMITTED at exit 0. Collateral is not a defence, and this sweep measured that rather than assuming it.

budget.decision: Swept exhaustively. The corpus turned out to be far cheaper than the brief's worst case because the slow paths are the --selftest paths, and the class under measurement is reachable on the ordinary (no-argument) run. Every checker was therefore run in its ordinary mode, which is also the mode in which a planted artifact would be admitted.

sweptExhaustively.dynamicDecodeProbe: 92 of 92 checkers, all completed, none timed out (420s cap).
sweptExhaustively.baselineRun: 92 of 92 checkers, all completed within a 300s cap. Slowest: check-evidence-v10.py 147.4s, check-c2-v9.py 107.7s, check-c2-v8.py 105.2s, check-versioning-v12.py 72.3s.
sweptExhaustively.liveExploit: 161 (checker, input, key) positions across 91 of 92 checkers, each run under attack shape A and again under the stronger order-preserving shape C, plus 5 additional nested-path positions in versioning-policy.v12.json. Exploit-phase checker executions: 143 (shape A) + 143 (shape C) + 18 (supplementary candidates, shape C) + 5 (nested paths) = 309. Plus 92 baseline runs and 92 instrumented probe runs: 493 checker executions in total.

sampled.nestedPathPositions: Nested (non-top-level) duplication was confirmed on 5 paths in versioning-policy.v12.json only (agentProtocolNote.position, custodyClasses, dischargeStatus, comparisonSchema, conformanceTests). All 5 ADMITTED at exit 0. The other 41 admitted artifacts were attacked at a top-level key only. The nested result is therefore a demonstration that the class is not confined to top-level keys, NOT a measured per-artifact nested rate.
sampled.keySelection: One key per (checker, input): the first of role, status, verdict, outcome, conclusion, decision, disposition, scope, version, claim, assurance, seal, acceptance, state, contract, artifact, id present at top level, else the first top-level key. Other keys at the same position were not enumerated.

skipped.selftestModes: No checker was run with --selftest. The brief's ~47min check-c2-v9.py figure and check-evidence-v10.py's ~42k cases are selftest-path costs. Skipping them means this sweep does not measure whether a checker's OWN selftest would catch a duplicate key, only whether its ordinary admission path does.
skipped.checkAdjudication: check-adjudication.py exits 2 at baseline before reaching any JSON artifact and no JSON input could be attributed to it, so no exploit case was constructed. Its single parse site is unhooked by static measure.
skipped.nonCheckerReaders: Only artifacts/check-*.py were swept. Other Python under docs/coop, and any human or tool that reads these artifacts outside a checker, were not measured.

exploitablePositions.note: The full enumerated list, per freeze 7.2 — a count is not a record. Each row is one (checker, input artifact, duplicated key) at which a single artifact-only insert was ADMITTED. parseInvisible means a last-wins parse of the mutant equals a last-wins parse of the honest document; orderPreserved means the dict key order is identical too.

2 finding(s) in versioning-policy.v4.json:

alreadyClosed.note: The adoption baseline. These checkers carry the fix and it was observed to FIRE against a live planted duplicate — not merely present in source.

uniformityOfTheFix.shape: Near-uniform. Every one of the 51 checkers that carries the fix installs an object_pairs_hook that walks the pair list and detects a repeated key. Two strategies exist: the common one RAISES on the first repeat; check-c2-v7/v8/v9.py instead RECORD the repeated keys into a side table so the checker can emit a C2Vn-DUPKEY finding that names the key and the file. Both close the class; the recording form gives the better finding.

reportedFindingNamesTheOffendingKey.reading: Two distinct causes. In check-operability-v8/v9/v10 the HOOK ITSELF is generic (_input_error / TransportInputError with a fixed 'duplicate object member' string), so the key is never captured. In check-trusted-request-context*.py and check-rust-provider-protocol.py the hook DOES name the key but the reporting layer prints only the exception class or a fixed sentence, so the key is captured and then discarded. Both reject; neither tells a reader WHERE.

alternativeClosureObserved.check-d9-v1.12.py: Does not hook _top_level_raw_value / _array_raw_elements — these call json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode unhooked. They are a lexer, not an admission path: the decoded value is discarded (_value) and only the byte span is kept. Duplicate keys are nonetheless refused there by a separate mechanism — _top_level_raw_value counts occurrences of the needle and raises 'top-level raw member {key!r} count=N' when N != 1. That closure is byte-positional and depends on the exact two-space-indent spelling of the needle, so it is narrower than an object_pairs_hook.

isThisSystemicOrConfinedToTwoLineages.verdict: SYSTEMIC, and materially wider than the two lineages in which it has been found.
evidence: 40 of 92 checkers admit a planted duplicate key at 59 enumerated positions across 42 distinct artifacts.

Those artifacts span at least 14 independent contract families — c2, d9, versioning, evidence, operability, delivery, threat-model, fact-plane, fact-identity, resolved-inputs, claim-register, retention-tiers, phase1a-a-prime-successor, scope-correction, product-dispositions, assurance-state and r1 — not two.

The C-2 and versioning lineages are where it was FOUND, not where it lives. C-2 is in fact one of the better-defended lineages now: v7, v8 and v9 all reject with a C2Vn-DUPKEY finding that names the key.

thePartitionIsCleanAndThatIsTheFinding.observed: Zero checkers have both an ADMITTED position and a duplicate-key-guarded position. A checker either carries the hook and rejects everywhere it was attacked, or carries no hook and admits.
thePartitionIsCleanAndThatIsTheFinding.reading: This is not a subtle partial-coverage problem. It is a binary adoption gap. Nothing needs to be invented: the primitive is already written 51 times in this same directory, in the same shape, and it fires. The gap is that 40 checkers never picked it up.

halfClosure.definition: The brief asks whether a checker hooks its own candidate but not its pinned inputs. In this corpus the sharper form is transitive: checkers import their predecessors and execute the predecessors' parses in-process.

worstExamples.check-evidence-v10.py: 0 unhooked decodes of its own; 280 unhooked decodes executed on a normal run through check-d9-v1.12.py, check-evaluation-proof.py and check-versioning-v5/v6/v7/v8.py.
worstExamples.check-d9-v1.14.py: 0 unhooked decodes of its own; 170 unhooked decodes through check-d9-v1.12.py. This is the checker check-versioning-v12.py subprocesses on every run and the one cited as carrying the fix — it does carry it, and it still runs 170 unhooked decodes.

widestSingleUnhookedSite.why: It is the binding grammar for preimage tagging. One unhooked parse, reached in-process by many unrelated checkers.

indirectionEvasionCheck.note: C-2 v8's review found a naive scan misses json.JSONDecoder().decode, raw_decode and getattr(json,'loads'). This sweep looked for all three in the AST and also instrumented them at runtime.
indirectionEvasionCheck.found: The only checker performing JSON decoding through indirection outside a string literal is check-d9-v1.12.py (json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode at L799 and L822, plus a decoder bound to a variable). No checker in this corpus reaches json.loads via getattr; the getattr spellings in check-c2-v8.py and check-c2-v9.py are inside string constants those checkers compile as test material for their own AST scanner, not live call sites.
indirectionEvasionCheck.runtimeConfirmation: The dynamic probe wrapped JSONDecoder.decode and JSONDecoder.raw_decode as well as json.loads/json.load, so an indirect decode would have been counted even if the AST scan had missed it. Across 92 instrumented runs the only decoder-level sites observed were check-d9-v1.12.py's two.

collateralIsNotADefence.measured: 55 positions rejected for a reason that is not a duplicate-key guard. Of these the overwhelming majority are sha/pin/drift comparisons on an input the checker pins by digest.
collateralIsNotADefence.aDigestPinIsARealButDifferentBarrier: It stops the one-file edit on a PINNED input, because the attacker would also have to edit the pin, which lives in the checker. It does nothing for a checker's own CANDIDATE, which is the artifact under review and is not pinned by the instrument reviewing it. Every ADMITTED position in this sweep is on an unpinned input.
collateralIsNotADefence.andTwoOfThemWereNotEvenThat: check-d9-v1.7.py's two positions rejected only on key ORDER and flipped to exit 0 under the order-preserving shape. Reading the exit code there would have produced a false 'closed'.

adoptionOrder.note: Checkers that should adopt the fix first, ordered by measured exposure: number of ADMITTED positions, then unhooked decodes actually executed on a normal run.

singleWorstFinding.why: It is the only checker in the corpus that both admits a planted duplicate at every position tested AND prints a coverage banner asserting total observation of the surface the plant sits in.

bannerPrintedWhileAPlantedDuplicateWasIn: PASS: versioning-policy.v12.json; every position outside successorRevision.proseAuthorityRepair, role, knownLimitations and the three successor-identity leaves is carried byte-identical from versioning-policy.v11.json and gated against those bytes
coverage census: 3600 leaf positions in the whole contract — 0 ungated
prose authority: 2829 string leaves — 361 RENDERED, 2468 CARRIED, 0 FREE
append admission: 0 of 361 authored string positions over 2 wordings, and 0 of 12 x 10 over the re-wording test set
measured.theContradiction: The banner says every position is 'carried byte-identical' and 'gated against those bytes', and that 0 of 3600 leaf positions are ungated. The gate is executed on the PARSED value, not on the bytes. A 107-byte insert changes the bytes at a gated position and the gate does not fire, because after json.loads the parsed value is unchanged. This is the corpus's dominant failure mode named in freeze 7 — a surface publishing a coverage claim over a region its instrument could not observe — and here the instrument's own banner is the claim.

blastRadiusOfTheCandidate.note: 671 objects independently reproduces the reviewer's reported figure for this artifact.

measured.itsOwnPinnedPredecessorIsNotExposedTheSa: versioning-policy.v11.json is sha-pinned by check-versioning-v12.py and the same attack there is rejected on the digest. The exposure is on the candidate, which is exactly the artifact under review.
measured.andItInheritsMore: On a normal run check-versioning-v12.py executes 974 unhooked decodes of its own plus 453 inherited from check-versioning-v5/v6/v7/v8/v9/v10/v11.py and check-evaluation-proof.py — including 359 unhooked decodes of claim-register.v1.json through check-versioning-v11.py:341.

blastRadius.note: Every object in an admitted artifact is a position at which a duplicate member could be planted. This is the structural upper bound, not a per-position measured admission rate; only 6 nested positions were executed (all in versioning-policy.v12.json, all admitted).

whatIDidNotCheck: No checker was run with --selftest. Whether a checker's own selftest would catch a planted duplicate is unmeasured for all 92.

Nested (non-top-level) duplication was executed on only 5 paths, all in versioning-policy.v12.json. The other 41 admitted artifacts were attacked at one top-level key each. The blast-radius object counts are a structural bound, not a measured nested admission rate.
One key per (checker, input) was attacked. Other keys at the same position, and duplicate keys inside arrays of objects, were not enumerated.
check-adjudication.py was not exploit-tested: it exits 2 at baseline before reaching a JSON artifact and no JSON input could be attributed to it.

The dynamic probe instruments the checker's own process. Parses performed in a SUBPROCESS a checker spawns were not instrumented, so inherited-decode counts are a lower bound for any checker that shells out rather than imports.

Per-parse-site file attribution records the FIRST text decoded at each site. A site that decodes several different artifacts is attributed to one of them, so 'ownParsedJsonInputs' understates breadth. This was partly compensated by adding 18 name-derived candidate cases, but no exhaustive per-site input enumeration was done.

14 checkers are already non-zero at baseline for unrelated reasons. For those, ADMITTED means the mutation produced output byte-identical to baseline (the instrument did not observe it); it does not mean the checker printed a green banner.

Only artifacts/check-*.py were swept. Other readers of these artifacts — other Python in the tree, and any human or tool reading them directly — were not measured, and they are the party the split actually deceives.
No repair was attempted, proposed in code, or applied. Nothing was sealed, signed or advanced.
